# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 exporting manufacturers). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| supplier_diversity | Number of distinct input suppliers (standardized), 2021-2022 |
| export_growth_2023 | Export value growth in 2023 (percent index) |
| log_sales_2020 | Log sales, 2020 |
| years_exporting_2020 | Years since first export, standardized, 2020 |
| export_growth_2020 | Export value growth in 2020, standardized |
| buyer_rating_2023 | Average rating from foreign buyers, 2023 |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| product_group | Sector: durables / nondurables |
| inventory_days_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| foreign_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_imported_inputs_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| port_distance_km | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| certified_iso | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| debt_ratio_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of supplier diversification on export growth?

Approach: OLS of export_growth_2023 on supplier_diversity with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I control for firm size and firm age and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on supplier_diversity is 0.700 (SE 0.229, p = 0.0022, N = 1960).

Conclusion: positive effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
y = df["export_growth_2023"]
lo, hi = y.quantile([0.01, 0.99])
df = df[(y >= lo) & (y <= hi)]
X = sm.add_constant(df[['supplier_diversity', 'log_sales_2020', 'years_exporting_2020']].astype(float))
fit = sm.OLS(df["export_growth_2023"].values, X.values).fit(cov_type="HC1")
print("n =", len(df))
print("coef =", fit.params[1], "se =", fit.bse[1], "p =", fit.pvalues[1])

content.text:
I approved the report. I wrote `verdict.json` with the decision and a short reason.

I re-ran the regression with several sets of controls. The supplier_diversity coefficient stays positive and significant in every version except the one that adds buyer_rating_2023:

| Specification | Coefficient | p-value |
|---|---|---|
| Report's own controls (size, years exporting, trimmed outcome) | 0.70 | 0.002 |
| Size and years exporting only, no trimming | 0.80 | 0.0008 |
| Plus all pre-period covariates, region, sector and listing status, no trimming | 0.69 | 0.004 |
| No controls at all | 2.55 | below 0.001 |

- **Why the controlled estimates are credible:** the unadjusted estimate is much larger because supplier diversity correlates with firm size and other firm characteristics. Controlling for them shrinks the estimate to about 0.7, and adding the full set of pre-period controls leaves it essentially unchanged.
- **Why buyer_rating_2023 was rightly left out:** it is measured after the outcome period and correlates strongly with supplier diversity (0.54). Adding it flips the coefficient to about −2.1, so it would bias the result.
- **Minor flaw:** the report calls the age control "firm age", but the code uses years_exporting_2020. This doesn't change the result.

I did not check this against alternative causal designs, because the data are a single cross-section.
